standard_prerequisites.name: Godel numbering of sequences
standard_prerequisites.statement: Finite sequences are coded by prime-power products; (y)_i is the i-th component of the code y, len(y) its length, and concatenation of coded symbol blocks is primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: A formation sequence is coded as y = <G(s_0), ..., G(s_{k-1})>, and the proof reads off its entries and length (733-741).

standard_prerequisites.name: Variable and constant tests
standard_prerequisites.statement: Var(x) and Const(x), deciding whether x codes a variable or a constant symbol, are primitive recursive (the unit establishes them just before the counted proposition).
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the first two clauses of the formation-rule condition on each entry (y)_i (738-740).

standard_prerequisites.name: Primitive recursive relations and bounded quantification
standard_prerequisites.statement: Relations built from primitive recursive functions, relations and bounded quantification are primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof stresses that the formation-sequence condition must be expressed with bounded quantifiers only, and the bounds come from the components of y (727-732, 744-752).

standard_prerequisites.name: Concatenation coding routine flatten
standard_prerequisites.statement: The routine flatten turning the code of a sequence of Godel numbers into the Godel number of the concatenated symbol string is primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: It appears inside clause (3) building (y)_i from the function symbol and the argument terms (743-747); the author flags it inline and makes its primitivity a follow-up problem, so the counted proof uses it as a standard coding routine.

core_obligations: Fix the format: a formation sequence s_0, ..., s_{k-1} = s records how s is built from variables and constants by the term-formation rules, coded by y with entries (y)_i (714-726).

Express 'y codes a formation sequence for the term with Godel number x' primitive recursively: for each i < k the entry (y)_i is a variable, a constant, or is built from terms coded by earlier entries using an n-place function symbol, the last clause written with flatten and bounded search over indices and components below y (727-752).
Add the closing condition (y)_{k-1} = x and replace k by len(y) so everything is bounded by y (748-752).

Bound y primitive recursively: a formation sequence for s has at most len(x) terms since subterms start at distinct places of s, each subterm has Godel number at most x, so a code exists that is at most p_{k-1}^{k(x+1)} with k = len(x) (754-762).
Obtain ClTerm from Term by dropping the variable clause (764-766).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up formation sequences and the shape of their codes.
Write the formation-rule condition as a primitive-recursive relation with bounded quantifiers.
Derive the primitive-recursive bound on the code of a formation sequence.
Get the closed-term relation by deleting the variable clause.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 707-712: the relations Term and ClTerm, which hold of the Godel number of a term or a closed term, are primitive recursive. The author proof (714-766) must encode formation sequences for terms, show that the three formation rules translate into primitive-recursive conditions on the code y of a candidate sequence using bounded quantification, derive a primitive-recursive bound on the code from the fact that every subterm starts at a distinct place inside s and has Godel number at most x, and finally obtain ClTerm by dropping the variable clause. The bound argument and the three-clause decomposition are real coding work, and the only deferred item is the auxiliary flatten routine whose primitivity the author flags inline and makes a follow-up problem.
